Engine: بدائية = her وردانية (12:13); فعلاً = فعلين (13:42); يدايقوكي = يضايقوكي (25:14); دولت = his ضلت (12:34); 'situation' at 06:47 = ستة وعشرين (Amal said she only repeated him, not a slip). Repeated root-letter swap سكر/كسر (29:46, 34:20, 43:00, 52:36) and زعمت/عزمت written as vocab-A tier 2 because Amal voiced each fix; a judge may move them to S4. air conditioning not on her sheet - no tier 3. coverage.r2: Whole file read in order. English-only stretches: 03:40-05:51 (recording-system talk), 17:06-18:06 (Amal explains pairs), 46:08-47:58 (when to use bnkeser), 57:37-1:02:33 (causative-verb wrap-up). echo: 'Intayn ila tult.' (07:20) = تنتين إلا تلت (his Latin-letter Arabic); 'Asha tisa alfayn situation' (06:47) = عشرة تسعة ألفين ستة وعشرين (Amal 06:54 'I just repeated what you said' - no slip); 'His cups broke' (39:45) and 'Their intention' (24:18) are real English. Engine garbles on AMAL's lines used for context: 12:13 بدائية = وردية (her feminine recast), 13:42 أههم بس فعلاً = بس فعلين, 38:33 أشياءي نوع الإل = أشيائي بدون الـ, 39:58 كساته = كاساته, 43:04 شو بدم كمان مرة = شو بدك كمان مرة, 45:57 بتنكسر = بننكسر (she supplied the i7na form before he tried). 55:30 Medi بفيت / 55:33 Amal أنا واعي unreadable, skipped. Not written: 03:11/03:13 وجهّزت and 03:18 are Amal repeating him (she agreed to stop repeating), 07:08 تلات إلا تلت -> تنتين إلا تلت is a wrong clock fact not a language slip, 15:02 أزعشتك (ج->ش) S4, 26:54 بعيم (ق dropped) S4, 35:45 أجر for إجر S4, 52:52 her إشي for his اشي is vowel/pronunciation, 40:30 كاسته 'his cup' vs her 40:34 كاسه is most likely the engine (كاستو by A3) so no row, 13:37 بنزعوج/بزعوج self-fixed in the same turn (GR-22), 51:44 بكسور->بكسر self-fixed, 49:31 من الحرارة->من الشوب self-fixed. Second repeats of a fixed line not written: 20:29 بيزعجيني (same as 19:59), 49:28 إن كسر (same as 48:41), 08:12 صلاحتو (same as 08:08), 40:35 كاسته.

r3_note: D5/D6 are one moment with two real slips (D3 grammar صلحني -> صلح لي; vocab صلح -> ساعدني) - I assigned D5 = grammar, D6 = vocab so they do not duplicate. Invented broken plurals (D8, D14) filed as vocab tier 2 per the reader brief; singular-for-plural (D12) as grammar A9. Rule questions (D18, D22, D23) dropped per the 2026-10-01 rule.

rows.why: He said za3amt (letters swapped) for 3azamt 'I invited'; Amal prompted him to try again then gave عزمت, and at 04:05 he himself names it as the word she corrected (same shape as the 09-26 دبا/بدا wrong-form ruling, not S4).

rows.medi_said: سـ... تلات إلا نـ... إلا تلت.
rows.why: Asked the time, he gave تلات (three) for the hour; Amal queried 'three or two?', he changed to تنتين إلا تلت and she repeated it. Low: the real clock time is not in the transcript, so it may be a fact slip rather than a word slip.
rows.r3_why: Amal's question 'تلات أو تنتين؟' is a voiced prompt and he switched to her number; kept low because the real time cannot be checked.

rows.why: Amal asked كيف الجو عندكم اليوم in the afternoon and he answered 'tonight' (الليلة); best reading is he meant today. Could be the engine or a real 'tonight'; she let it pass.
rows.r3_why: Plausible wrong word she let pass; vocab-B goes to her review, kept low.

rows.why: Levantine says a video على YouTube, not لـ; Amal let it pass (best reading).
rows.english: I watched a video on YouTube

rows.why: He made a non-form صلاحتو for 'I fixed it'; Amal recast صلحته.
rows.r3_challenge: صلاحتو vs صلحته differs only in a long vowel (salaa7to / salla7to) - may be S4 pronunciation or engine spelling rather than a wrong form.

rows.why: Sheet: 'i call | Ana barenn (3ala)' - rann takes 3ala, he used la-; Amal was busy with the electricity word and let it pass.
rows.r3_why: Fixed preposition of rann is 3ala (sheet); she let it pass.

rows.medi_said: Is it را-- راكي؟ What, What was electricity?
rows.why: He could not find the word for electricity and asked; Amal supplied كهربا (sheet: electricity | Kahraba | كهربا).

rows.medi_said: كراجي. See, This is a new word.
rows.why: He garbled the word Amal had given at 09:10 (كهربجي, also said as كرهبجي at 09:30); she recast it syllable by syllable. He attempted it, so not tier 0; wrong form of a word just given = tier 2.
rows.r3_why: He attempted the word and mangled it, Amal recast - tier 2, not a didn't-know (tier 0 is for a word he never tried).

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- لا، أه، كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.why: He meant 'he is not an electrician, he is an engineer': a noun is negated with mish and no 'to be' verb (مش كهربجي); he built ما يكون. Best reading of a halting turn; Amal let it pass.
rows.english: he's not an electrician, he's an engineer
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the slip; the sentence contrasts with present هو مهندس, so present negation of a noun (C4, مش) fits better than past ما كان (B6).

rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. Like you, you were who's being fixed. ... Fixed for me، صلح لي.
rows.why: 'for me' rides on the preposition la- with an ending (صلح لي), not on the verb as its object (صلحني = he fixed ME); Amal explained the difference out loud.
rows.english: he fixed it for me a bit
rows.r3_why: Same moment holds TWO real slips; D5 and D6 are the same pair with labels swapped. I rule D5 = the grammar slip (صلحني -> صلح لي, D3) and D6 = the vocab slip (صلح -> ساعدني) so neither is duplicated.

rows.medi_said: صلح لي, helps to me, شوي.
rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me? ... ساعدني.
rows.why: He used صلح (fix) meaning 'he helped me' (he said 'helps to me'); Amal asked if he meant help and he produced ساعدني, which she repeated (sheet: help | Saa3ed | ساعد).
rows.r3_why: See D5: this is the second, separate slip of the same moment - the wrong verb.

rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour adjective is وردانية; Amal recast (engine wrote بدائية) and he said 'وردانية that's right'.

For 'I stayed' the doubled verb dall takes the -ait ending (ضلّيت, sheet: i stayed/kept | Ana dallait); he said a dallet-type form (engine wrote دولت), Amal did not recognise it ('what?') and gave ضليت, he repeated it. The verb is right, only the past ending is wrong, so grammar not vocab.
rows.r3_why: The word is right (ضل), only the past ending is off - a B5 ending rule, so grammar per the brief, not tier 2.

rows.medi_said: اه، this is take على بيتي.
rows.why: He used على for 'at my house'; Amal prompted 'بِ or فِي بيتي?' and he fixed to في بيتي.
وحدة (one) goes after the noun like an adjective; Amal recast بس كلمة وحدة.

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.amal_said: أههم بس فعلاً. (engine; she said فعلين)
rows.why: Two takes the dual form fe3lain, not fe3el + tnain; Amal gave the dual and he repeated فعلين at 13:46.
She asked for 'you (f) got annoyed with me'; he stalled in English and she supplied انزعجتي one second later - a didn't-know, not a slip.
rows.r3_why: Amal supplied the form before any attempt = didn't-know, tier 0.

rows.medi_said: نز، نزعجتي، معي انزعجتي، مع، معي
rows.amal_said: ليش ما؟ ... You were annoyed with me.
rows.why: انزعج takes من (Amal at 14:35: 'you would say مِنْ'); she questioned his مع and he fixed to انزعجتي مني ('Perfect').

He asked how to say 'one more' with a word-for-word guess (aktar); Amal gave كمان واحد (sheet: one more time | Kaman marra) and he repeated. Framed as a how-do-you-say question, so a didn't-know (tier 0).
rows.r3_why: It is a 'how do you say' question with a guess; brief files that as vocab-A tier 0 asked.

rows.why: Speaking to a woman (إنتي) the adjective must be feminine; Amal asked 'إنتي or انت?' and he fixed to مزعوجة.
'Many things annoy me' needs the plural verb بزعجوني; Amal recast and he said 'Oh yeah, it's plural'. He repeated the slip at 20:29, fixed again - one row.
rows.english: many things annoy me these days

rows.why: He said ayoom for the broken plural ayyaam; Amal supplied أيام and he took it ('I even wrote أيام'). The brief puts an invented plural shape under vocab tier 2 (the fix is a pattern, not an ending rule). Could be only a vowel slip.
rows.r3_why: Broken-plural shape wrong; the reader brief lists 'wrong plural pattern he invented' as vocab tier 2.

rows.medi_said: إنتي متأكدة إلي إنتو ما ازعج، از- ازعجتو.
rows.why: 'Sure that ...' takes إنو, not اللي; Amal asked 'Why اللي?' and said 'إنو مش اللي'.
rows.english: are you sure that you didn't annoy him?

rows.why: 'You didn't annoy HIM' needs the object ending -ه on the verb; Amal let it pass (best reading).
rows.r3_challenge: ازعجتو is how ازعجتوه is pronounced (az3ajtu, the final -h is silent); the transcript cannot show a missing object ending - likely engine spelling, not a slip.

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا the verb keeps its b-; Amal recast إذا ما بشوف and he repeated إذا ما بشوفك مبسوطة.
rows.english: if I don't see you happy

rows.why: For 'don't be annoyed' he gave the positive command إنزعجي; Amal prompted 'So don't be' and he gave ما تنزعجي.
In 'it wasn't their intention to upset you' the second verb drops b-; Amal recast يضايقوكي (engine wrote يدايقوكي) over his بيضايقوكي (engine wrote بيتايوكي).

rows.medi_said: So I add is بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: He gave a wrong form بزياد for 'I add'; Amal recast بزيد and he repeated it.
He asked the verb for 'to remove'; Amal supplied بقيم.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: 'The beginning of the word' is awal el-kelme - no el- before awal (A13); he put el- on awal both times. Low: he often uses a bare الـ as a filler, so the first الـ may be a pause (S5). Amal only said Mm.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / word
rows.r3_why: Repeated el- before awal in both phrases suggests a real A13 slip, but filler الـ is possible - kept low.

rows.why: He named K-S-R then said بخسر (a different word, 'I lose') for بكسر 'I break'; Amal said 'close' and gave بكسر. Kept as tier 2 to match the agreed كسر/سكر letter-swap rows (A19, A21, A24, A29).
rows.r3_why: Same family as the agreed letter-swap rows; she voiced the fix, so it stays vocab-A tier 2.

rows.why: Letters swapped: sakkarti (you closed) for kasarti (you broke); Amal recast and he repeated كسرتي twice.
A plain present verb takes b- (بيكسروا), as in all his other forms; Amal said Nice and let it pass.

After بتضلي the second verb needs its person prefix; he said bare كسري three times, Amal recast بتكسري and said she did not hear the t, he fixed to بتكسري at 33:31. The missing piece she named is the t (person), so B18; the b- is the second issue.
rows.r3_why: Amal named the missing t, so B18 is the main bucket; B1 as second id.

rows.medi_said: Is it يسكر and يسكري؟ اسكرو؟ إسكر.
rows.amal_said: The K is before the S.
rows.why: Letters swapped again (eskor = close) for the command 'break' (eksor); Amal named it: 'The K is before the S', he fixed to اكسري، اكسروا.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; Amal said 'no el' and he said كل أشيائي.
'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he used the singular كاسته, Amal recast and he said 'كاساته، of course'. Choosing singular for plural is a number slip (A9), not an invented word form.
rows.r3_why: He knows both forms (he says 'of course'); singular used for plural = A9 grammar.

rows.why: كاسة is feminine so the verb is انكسرت; Amal recast and he said 'Oh, 'cause it's female'.

rows.amal_said: شو بدم كمان مرة؟ ... صح، بس order. Word or letters order.
rows.why: Letters swapped a third time (insakarat for inkasarat); Amal asked him to repeat and named the letter order; he fixed at 43:16.
The sentence was 'when she was 12'; he said eleven and Amal recast إتناش, which he used at 44:18.
For هو the verb is بينكسر without the feminine -i; Amal moved on to إنتو without fixing it. Low: could be the engine carrying the -i from the previous إنتي بتنكسري line.
rows.r3_why: Real agreement slip in a conjugation drill that Amal let pass (her next word إنتو just moves the drill on).

rows.why: byinkeser is the huwwe form; for heyye it is btinkeser; Amal prompted 'هو' (that's the he-form) and he fixed: هي بتنكسر (45:46). His 45:24 هو بينكسري (ي ending on the he-form) went by with her 'إنتو' only.

rows.medi_said: air condition-ي، air conditioner-ي. Do I say for air condition?
rows.why: A borrowed English noun takes 'my' with taba3i, not the -i ending; he produced the -i form first, then asked, and Amal gave the taba3i form, which he used at 48:31 and 53:14. Low because the attempt turned into a question.
rows.r3_why: He produced the wrong form before asking, and she recast it - kept, low.

rows.medi_said: الـ air conditioning تبعي ... انكسر انكسر؟
rows.amal_said: If it's physically broke then it's this. If it's not working properly we'd need that other word

rows.r3_challenge: He asked 'انكسر؟' and Amal said at 49:51 'You would use انكسر' if it really broke; she only explained the خرب option - not clearly a correction of a wrong word.

rows.medi_said: أبدًا، ما بـ... بكسر، أنا ما بكسر، اشي
rows.why: 'I have never broken anything' is past; Amal asked 'بكسر or كسرت?' and explained أبداً only needs ما; he said أنا أبدًا ما كسرت ولا اشي.
Letters swapped again (sakkart = I closed) for kasart; Amal recast and he repeated كسرت at 52:44.
'I didn't sleep well' negates the verb with ma; he negated the adverb with mish; Amal recast with 'Or' (may be offering the better form rather than ruling his wrong) and he repeated ما نِمِت منيح.

rows.medi_said: إن إن. الفـ--، الفـ--، علات، الفعلات إن.
rows.why: He invented the plural fe3laat for fe3el; Amal gave the broken plural أفعال and he said الأفعال. Invented plural pattern = vocab tier 2 per the brief.
rows.r3_why: Invented plural pattern; brief puts this under vocab tier 2.

rows.why: For 'I am annoyed' he said مزعج (annoying); his 'No.' gave no right word before Amal supplied أنا مزعوج, then he confirmed مزعج = annoying. Sheet: annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج; annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج. Same root, wrong participle of a word he knows (he said مزعوج at 18:41) = tier 2.
rows.r3_why: Not a self-fix (no right word before hers); wrong participle of a known word = tier 2.
